title: Household-level poverty can conceal unequal access to health, internet, property, and decision power within the same family
source_unit: Asian Development Bank, Key Indicators for Asia and the Pacific 2026
geography: Asia and the Pacific; theme analysis of 23 developing economies and statistical indicators for 50 ADB regional member economies

denominator.unit: developing economies in the report's thematic analysis of deprivation

dual_lens.value: The report combines shared household circumstances with individual experiences to measure socioeconomic deprivation

hidden_deprivation.value: A substantial share of people experience individual deprivation while living in households that are not classified as poor

resource_distribution.value: People in the same household do not necessarily share the same opportunities, resources, or decision-making power

measurement_meaning.value: Household averages can hide who receives capability, access, and agency within the household

observations.method: ADB thematic analysis combining household-level and individual-level deprivation indicators across 23 developing economies in Asia and the Pacific.
observations.uncertainty: The report's individual deprivation measures and country coverage do not establish causal household bargaining processes or imply that every non-poor household contains the same pattern of hidden deprivation.
observations.subgroup: Women, men, children, working-age adults, older people, rural and urban residents, and individuals within households with different resource and decision positions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Household pooling can provide protection and shared resources; individual deprivation indicators identify unequal outcomes but do not by themselves show whether intra-household allocation, external institutions, or personal needs are the main cause.

observations.period: 2026 report; demographic and spatial inequality in individual deprivation

denominator.unit: developing economies in the report's thematic analysis

gender_pattern.value: Women are consistently identified among groups experiencing greater individual deprivation

rural_pattern.value: Rural residents are consistently identified among groups experiencing greater individual deprivation

age_pattern.value: People ages 25–39 are consistently identified among groups experiencing greater individual deprivation

intersectional_meaning.value: Deprivation risk is shaped by gender, place, and life stage in ways that household poverty status alone may not reveal

observations.method: ADB cross-country comparison of individual deprivation indicators disaggregated by demographic and spatial groups.
observations.uncertainty: The summary reports consistent group patterns but not a single causal estimate; group averages can conceal within-group variation, country differences, and measurement differences across indicators.
observations.subgroup: Women, rural residents, people ages 25–39, urban residents, men, other age groups, and people at different stages of household formation and work.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher measured deprivation among a group does not mean all members lack agency or resources; some indicators may reflect life-stage needs, survey design, or country-specific opportunity structures.

observations.period: 2026 report; health, digital, and property access as capability conditions

denominator.unit: developing economies in the report's thematic analysis

health_insurance.value: Lack of health insurance is identified as a key driver of deprivation

internet_access.value: Lack of internet access is identified as a key driver of deprivation

property_ownership.value: Lack of property ownership is identified as a key driver of deprivation

capability_route.value: Health protection, connectivity, and ownership shape individual capability and decision power beyond household income alone

observations.method: ADB thematic analysis linking individual deprivation indicators with access to health insurance, internet, property, and other resources.
observations.uncertainty: The report identifies drivers and associations within a comparative measurement framework; the summary does not establish which access intervention would have the largest effect or how resources are controlled within households.
observations.subgroup: Individuals without health coverage, internet access, or property ownership, especially women, rural residents, and working-age adults in developing economies.
observations.counterinterpretation: Insurance, internet, and property can improve opportunity without guaranteeing agency or wellbeing; ownership and access may also be mediated by debt, quality, reliability, safety, and household control.

observations.period: 2026 report; statistical infrastructure and policy targeting

denominator.unit: ADB regional member economies included in the publication's statistical indicators

indicator_scope.value: The publication compiles economic, financial, social, environmental, labor, governance, globalization, transport, and communication indicators

policy_targeting.value: The thematic chapter calls for targeted, gender-sensitive, and individual-focused interventions rather than relying only on household-level poverty classification

data_gap.value: More granular individual measurement changes which people and mechanisms become visible to policy

development_meaning.value: Measurement architecture is part of social policy capacity: what is counted determines whether hidden deprivation can be reached

observations.method: ADB publication combining a thematic deprivation chapter with standardized indicators and economy tables for regional members.
observations.uncertainty: Statistical coverage, comparability, missingness, and indicator definitions vary across economies; better measurement does not itself deliver services, redistribution, or household decision power.
observations.subgroup: Statistical agencies, policymakers, service providers, households, individuals with hidden deprivation, and groups requiring gender- or place-sensitive targeting.
observations.counterinterpretation: Individual targeting can improve precision but may increase administrative burden, privacy risk, exclusion errors, or intra-household conflict if governance and recourse are weak.

boundary: This record adds an Asia-Pacific measurement-to-capability route from household poverty classification through individual deprivation, gender and rural inequality, health insurance, internet access, property ownership, decision power, and targeted policy. It uses ADB comparative indicators and a thematic deprivation framework; it is not a causal evaluation, a universal household survey, or proof that targeting produces realized agency or wellbeing.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official ADB Key Indicators for Asia and the Pacific 2026 page was reviewed for the 23-economy deprivation analysis, household/individual dual-lens framework, group patterns, deprivation drivers, 50-economy indicator scope, and policy implications.
